unknowns: Session label for 2 January 2025 (matches 93 and 94, both semi-finals) is not published in the Wikipedia schedule: that day's table is the only one carrying no session caption. Recorded as session: null rather than guessed. Both semi-finals were played on that single day.

Match 35 (Ian White v Sandro Eric Sosing, first round, 20 December 2024) was a walkover, so it has no set score and no leg scores. It is assigned to the 20 December afternoon session as printed in the schedule table, but no darts were thrown.
Per-set leg scores are published for all 94 played matches; the only null setScores is the walkover (match 35).

Exact clock start times per session are given by the source as 12:30 GMT (afternoon) and 19:00 GMT (evening), except the final at 19:30 GMT; these are not carried in this dataset beyond the afternoon/evening label.
notes: matchNo 1-95 is Wikipedia's own event-wide schedule numbering (chronological across the whole tournament, not restarted per round); it is unique and stable, and sessions[].matches reference it.

Beau Greaves (England) qualified via the Women's World Matchplay but DECLINED her place, choosing the 2024 WDF World Darts Championship after a PDC ruling barred playing both World Championships in the same year. She is therefore NOT among the 96 and does not appear in field[]. Her spot was reallocated to the PDC Tour Card Holder qualifier.
Two women did play: Noa-Lynn van Leuven (Netherlands) and Fallon Sherrock (England), both via the PDC Women's Series; both lost in the first round.

Dom Taylor was originally 17th on the Pro Tour list but was suspended by the Darts Regulation Authority after a failed drugs test; Robert Owen replaced him. Jeffrey de Graaf qualified via both the Pro Tour and PDC Nordic & Baltic and was drawn as a Pro Tour qualifier, so he is listed here under his drawn route (international qualifier / PDC Nordic & Baltic per the source's own qualifier list).

Source spelling inconsistencies normalised: 'Jeffrey De Graaf' -> 'Jeffrey de Graaf' and 'Dimitri Van Den Bergh' -> 'Dimitri Van den Bergh' (the source prints both casings). 'Mensur Suljovic' is printed WITHOUT diacritics in the source's qualifier list and schedule tables, so that is the form recorded here; his Wikipedia article title is the diacritic form 'Mensur Suljović'.
Verified: all 32 second-round matches pair exactly one of the 32 seeds against a first-round winner, and every round's entrants are exactly the previous round's winners.
Verified: for all 94 played matches, the per-set leg scores reconcile with the reported set score.
Non-playing days inside the tournament span are recorded in sessions[] with noPlay: true - 24, 25, 26 December 2024 (Christmas break) and 31 December 2024 (New Year's Eve).
